title: Foundations for Christian Technology
description: A Christian companion to the Center for Humane Technology's Foundations of Humane Technology: fifteen modules in five movements, walking the shape of the gospel story from lament to commissioning.
purpose: Upgrade the collective wisdom of the church to improve awareness and decision-making in a world facing emergent 'godlike' technology
thumbnailAlt: Foundations for Christian Technology course cover

contributorPresences.name: Matthew Dowell
contributorPresences.contribution: Author and steward of Foundations for Christian Technology. Adapted the Center for Humane Technology curriculum with biblical foundations and Christian theological integration.

contributorPresences.name: Tristan Harris
contributorPresences.contribution: Co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology. His work exposing the attention economy and advocating for humane technology provides the foundational structure and vision for this course.

contributorPresences.name: Aza Raskin
contributorPresences.contribution: Co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology. His systems thinking approach to technology ethics and work on AI safety deeply influenced the course's analytical framework.

contributorPresences.name: Randima (Randy) Fernando
contributorPresences.contribution: Executive Director of the Center for Humane Technology. His leadership in developing the Foundations of Humane Technology course provided the pedagogical structure adapted in this Christian edition.

contributorPresences.name: Daniel Schmachtenberger
contributorPresences.contribution: His work on the metacrisis, existential risk, and civilizational design directly inspired the 'A Problem Well Stated' module. His articulation of generator functions and systemic risk informs the course's analysis of technology's role in civilizational challenges.
